status: PROVISIONAL — not the committed R2 slice (Codex quota blocked)

q1_can_birth_be_reconstructed_from_descr.claim: A verifier CAN reconstruct the canonical Birth, its digest and its IdentityID from the BRQ1D descriptor bytes alone.

evidence.note: buildBirth() is a pure function of the two public keys plus fixed constants (type, v, suite, threshold 2, algorithm order), so nothing else is needed.

q2_what_does_the_digest_bind.claim: The carried digest is RECOMPUTABLE from the carried keys. It is a self-consistency / corruption check, NOT an external trust anchor.

evidence.substitution_test: a wholly different TEST identity descriptor (keys + its own matching digest) verifies internally
evidence.consequence: A verifier with no external anchor cannot tell the intended actor from a substituted one. Binding to a SPECIFIC intended actor requires an external anchor (e.g. the IdentityID/digest published in the authenticated authority log, or a signature over the descriptor digest).

q3_possession_authority_freshness.claim: The descriptor contains NO signature. It proves no proof of possession, no current authority and no freshness.

evidence.descriptor_layout: 5 ASCII bytes "BRQ1D" + 32-byte SHA3-256 canonical-Birth digest + 2592-byte ML-DSA-87 public key + 64-byte SLH-DSA-SHAKE-256s public key

q4_single_family_brq1m.claim: The single-family BRQ1M descriptor (2629 bytes: header + digest + ML public key only) CANNOT reconstruct the canonical Birth, so its advertised digest cannot be checked from its own contents.

evidence.verdict: The Layer-4 canonical Birth requires BOTH root public keys (2-of-2 dual family). A single-family descriptor therefore advertises a digest it cannot substantiate. BRQ1M is a diagnostic comparison only, not a construction.

offline_self_containment.supports: The descriptor alone rebuilds the canonical Birth, the IdentityID and both public keys offline, and can verify signatures made by those roots over a separately supplied message.
offline_self_containment.caveat: Verifying a separately supplied signed assertion is outside the one-QR-alone claim.

unknown_actor_current_authority.supports: NOT supported by any single descriptor. Determining current authority requires the authenticated append-only authority log (succession, revocation, root rotation), which a descriptor does not carry. R1 already recorded this limitation.

options: External trust anchor: publish the descriptor digest / IdentityID in the authenticated authority log so substitution is detectable against an independently obtained expected ID. No new algorithm, no new certificate.

Out-of-band signed public assertion: carry the descriptor digest + identity metadata plus an ML-DSA-87 signature over it, with the signature delivered out of band (log atom / link) rather than inside the same QR.

byte_budget_reality.note: R1 measured these on a real encoder: even the smallest standard NIST pk+signature package does not fit v40-L, and base64/base32 encodings of the descriptor do not fit at any EC level. Do not drop the dual-family requirement and do not invent a compression or packing scheme.

mutations.name: flip one byte of the carried digest
flip one byte of the ML public key
wholesale substitution with the other TEST identity descriptor
flip one byte of the private capsule entropy

detail.note: The capsule has no self-authenticating checksum, so a corrupted entropy silently yields a DIFFERENT (valid-looking) identity rather than an error. Detection must come from comparing the recovered IdentityID against an independently known expected ID.
